subject: Exec pulse: weekly wins, blockers, and QBR action lanes
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: leadership@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exec pulse: weekly wins, blockers, and QBR action lanes

Team —

Quick weekly dispatch ahead of next week's QBR prep meeting. I left the note focused on the few things I want leaders to digest and act on before Monday's dry run. TL;DR: momentum on throughput optimizations, at-risk item on Dedicated contract timeline, and two asks for leadership.

Wins
- Serving runtime 2.3 rollout: 12% median latency drop on long-tail workloads after kernel selection fix; infra metrics show steady throughput.
- Customer onboarding: AtlasHealth pilot ingested test workload; initial inference quality checks passed. Sara (Atlas) confirmed integration tests run.
- Cost profiling: initial Optimize suggestions reduced per-token cost by ~8% on the staging workload.

Risks / Blockers
- Dedicated capacity contract: procurement review at Atlas stalled on data retention clause. Legal needs a redline response by EOD Monday or we lose target deployment window.
- Telemetry gap: a subset of trace IDs from the new quantized model are not surfacing end-to-end in Console; could mask regressions during QBR demos.

Asks (concrete)
1) Laura — please own the Atlas procurement reply (legal cc). If we don't get the redline in by Mon 5/31 5pm PT, request to leadership for an SLA exception will be needed.
2) Karthik — can you prioritize the missing trace-ID reconciliation? A one-day spike to infra resources and an audit of the tracing shim should be enough; aim for a fix by EOD Monday.

Attachments: QBR_one_pager.pdf (one-pager outline for exec demo), cost-trend-snapshot.csv (per-model token cost last 30d).

Notes: I am scheduling a 30-min dry run Mon 10:00am PT — invite to follow.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec pulse: weekly wins, blockers, and QBR action lanes

Thanks for the crisp summary — appreciate the callouts. Quick responses inline.

> Dedicated capacity contract: procurement review at Atlas stalled on data retention clause.
I spoke with legal yesterday and copied the specific alternative language they can accept. I'll prepare a narrow redline that keeps our auditability requirements but clarifies retention windows for the pilot. Will share draft to Marissa and legal (legal@redwood.ai) by 3pm PT Friday so Atlas procurement has time to respond before Monday. If Atlas pushes for a full enterprise-retention exemption we escalate to product and leadership.

> Telemetry gap: subset of trace IDs not surfacing
This one is high priority for demo fidelity. Karthik — can you share an ETA here? If we need to surface a short-term mitigant, we can add a conditional comment in the demo script and ensure the mock trace is available.

Operational ask: please add the dry-run agenda to the Drive link you shared and mark any sections where leadership will be asked to sign off (pricing/commitment/SLAs).

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Product Operations
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 13:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec pulse: weekly wins, blockers, and QBR action lanes

On it. Short update: I reproduced the missing-span behavior locally (root cause: shim version mismatch in one of the inference workers). Hotfix plan:
- 1hr rolling update to align tracing shim (today afternoon)
- validation job to rehydrate and surface the missing trace IDs (overnight)
- confirm in Console by Mon 09:00 PT.

If the rolling update causes instability we'll fallback to mock-injection for demo lanes and move the real tracing rollout to the post-QBR window.

— Karthik
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai; Sara Voss <sara@atlashealth.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Exec pulse: weekly wins, blockers, and QBR action lanes

Forwarding final plan and two small updates for visibility to Sara at Atlas.

Laura — thanks for the redline timeline. Once you post the draft I will loop in Atlas procurement.
Karthik — appreciate the hotfix plan; please call out the rollback criteria in the dry-run notes.

Atlas / Sara — quick note for you: we expect the pilot contract redline in your procurement review next week. If you need a short call to walk through the data-retention language, happy to schedule 30m Mon or Tue.

Action items consolidated:
- Laura: post redline draft by 3pm PT today and add to the Drive folder.
- Karthik: complete shim alignment and validation job; confirm by Mon 09:00 PT.
- Neha: prep one slide on QBR ask (SLA vs pilot scope) for Monday's dry run.

Attachments attached here: QBR_one_pager.pdf (final deck outline) and cost-trend-snapshot.csv.

See Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/QBR-2027-Prep

Marissa
